analysis:
The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md (head lines 11-246): it renames the unpublished v0.10.1 candidate to v0.10.2 and adds release notes. It changes no executable code, so I found no new vulnerability, and the changelog carries no secrets. The notes describe source changes elsewhere that I could not inspect, so some security conclusions are unverified.

Relevant threat T-041 (prefix cache, TB-007, A-001):
- The notes describe Nemotron Super and GLM-5.3-Flash writing 4-bit `balanced` encrypted SSD checkpoints by default, in new cache namespaces. Old exact files miss once and then expire through the normal TTL sweep.
- Super now advertises prefix_cache_v2_models, so it receives a coordinator cache scope (account-derived salt) only after its tuple is allowlisted. This should be consistent with the cache-scope mitigation, but the code was not supplied.
- The SSD write-queue depth rises from 2 to 6 donations. The changelog says queued bytes stay within the existing cap.
- The notes say cache keys are replaced after a Secure Enclave key change and unreadable files are removed.
- Heartbeat status gains an optional `detail` field carrying a cause such as `key_unavailable`. This is minor metadata and the notes say it contains no request text.
- The notes describe new `darkbloom logs` refusal-reason lines and say they never contain request text.

Questions for integration, none of them provable from this diff:
- Whether the rewritten HMAC lookup-tag and namespace derivation still folds in cacheSalt.
- Whether the 4-bit layout metadata adds nothing prompt-derived to the AAD.
- Whether the new logprob exposure on Super and GLM changes the TTFT oracle.
- Whether the MLX, mlx-swift and mlx-swift-lm pin bumps (56 Metal kernel files) keep the signed-artifact, qualification and attestation contracts for T-034 and T-054 intact.
- Whether the new desktop release workflow, with its signing and notarization, is separately reviewed.

The actual code and submodule diffs need review. This changelog-only unit shows no regression.
